content: After updating to 4.31 rc2, I found some convert generating more goals than before. I saw them mostly rfl, mostly instance stuffs. Are we having a new set_option ... ? Is there a way I can (systematically) know this every time without asking somebody?
This comes from #39928 by @Anne Baanen
(the quick fix is to use convert! as is probably clear from the changes in that PR)
@Nailin Guan The reasoning is that those goals used to be "closed by rfl automatically" behind the scenes, but they can hide defeqs that lead to proofs that are hard to maintain.

Thank you all, I already got these from the PR description.
My only question left is probably how I can know this elsewhere? Since asking every time when there is a problem (when updating) doesn't seem a good choice.
How do you update? Do you use hopscotch? Because it will tell you the exact commit to Mathlib that is causing your bump problems. And then you can just look at that commit to see what changed.
#general > hopscotch: an interactive tool to bump Lean dependencies

There are some cases where the new convert is too weak, which we should fix

  1. My PR #38071 which was merged today causes convert to not anymore deal with congruence of overapplications, which I fixed in #40740.
  2. convert now always uses reducible transparency for subgoals, but this is not appropriate for implicit subgoals, where the transparency level should be bumped up. For example:
import Mathlib

example (a b c : ℝ) (h : a < b) : a < c := by
  rw [lt_iff_le_not_ge, ← lt_iff_le_not_ge]
  convert h
  -- ⊢ Real.instPreorder.toLT = Real.instLT
  -- ⊢ c = b

cc @Anne Baanen
@Jovan Gerbscheid, are you aware of #40663 ?
